text:
Maria (Support): Heads-up — we're doing a soft-launch of rate policy v2 (growth tier, 10% traffic) at 09:10 UTC and OrbitHealth just pinged with a spike of 429s starting ~09:12. Anyone watching the canary? :eyes:
Keon (Eng Platform): On it. Can you paste a sample request id + response headers when they hit a 429?
Maria (Support): Sample from customer logs:
> request_id: r-9a1b2c3d
> x-rate-limit-limit: 120
> x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
> x-rate-limit-reset: 1680000000
Response body: {"error":"quota_exhausted","policy":"v2"}
Jonas (Eng Oncall): Quick checks: is their token still mapped to Growth? If they've been re-tagged as Free we'll see much lower limits.
Priya (Customer Success): Confirmed — OrbitHealth is on Growth. They had a nightly batch job that spiked at 09:11. They say this job is unchanged.
Keon (Eng Platform): Looking at the canary dashboard — growth-tier (10% slice) shows 429s jump at 09:12 and token-burst-credit metric dropping to zero rapidly. Policy v2 changed backlog behavior to immediate reject when burst is exhausted. That lines up.
Keon (Eng Platform): Hypothesis: the new leaky-bucket parameters (burst=200, refill=10/s) plus zero-backlog means short sharp bursts exhaust budget and get rejected rather than queuing briefly.
Maria (Support): OrbitHealth needs quick relief — can we roll the canary back to 0% or patch config to smooth bursts?
ops-bot: @Keon acknowledged. Initiating rollback option check. (automated)
Keon (Eng Platform): I can either rollback the rollout to 0% (will revert all v2 behavior) or flip a canary config: set backlog_ms=50 and bump burst to 250 for the 10% slice. Prefer the latter to avoid full rollback while we validate.
Jonas (Eng Oncall): Agree with patched approach first. If 429s don't drop in 5m, escalate to full rollback. Watch p95 and 429/s.
Maria (Support): Deploy then and I'll tell OrbitHealth to retry.
deploy-bot: Applying config to cluster/canary-3: {"policy":"v2","target":"growth","slice":10,"backlog_ms":50,"burst":250} — rolling change now.
Keon (Eng Platform): Change applied to canary-3. Instrumenting a short trace to confirm path: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.prod/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' -v` -> check `x-rate-limit-*` headers.
Jonas (Eng Oncall): Monitoring: 429/s for canary group: 18 -> 3 within 90s. p95 latency increased by ~8–15ms.
Maria (Support): OrbitHealth reports immediate improvement, their retries are getting through now. :thumbsup:
Priya (Customer Success): I'll update the customer ticket and ask them to monitor the nightly job for the next 30m.
Keon (Eng Platform): Temporary mitigation looks effective. I'm pausing the progressive rollout (stop increase from 10% -> 30%). We'll keep canary at 10% with patched config until postmortem.
Maria (Support): Filed internal follow-up to capture lessons. We should document when to prefer shallow backlog vs immediate reject in rollout playbooks.
Jonas (Eng Oncall): Action items: 1) Add metric `burst_credit_drain_count` and alert if drain_count > 10/min for any slice. 2) Add trace span for "quota.refill" events.
Keon (Eng Platform): Filing RFC-5823: "v2 backlog vs reject semantics" and PR to add `burst_credit_drain_count` to telemetry. Tagging eng-runtime + eng-sre.
ops-bot: Rollback aborted — canary paused at 10% with patched config. (automated)
Maria (Support): Thanks team — will only close the escalation once Priya confirms no new 429s for 30m.
Priya (Customer Success): OrbitHealth confirmed no further 429s in the last 25m. Ticket updated and customer notified.
Maria (Support): Great. Postmortem + docs next week. Leaving this thread pinned for RFC linkage. :memo:
